_comment: Chronos Earth — curated battles dataset. See public/data/README.md for the schema. 'year' is a signed calendar year (negative = BCE). Casualty figures are rough historical estimates and vary by source. Add a battle by copying an entry. 'commanders' lists each side's leaders: side is 1 or 2 (matching belligerents), wiki is the English Wikipedia article title (used for the portrait + link; run scripts/fetch-portraits.mjs after adding). Set 'hasBattleView': true only if you also add phase data in battle-views.json.

battles.name: Battle of Ankara
battles.outcome: Timur's army beat the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I near Ankara. Bayezid was captured and died a prisoner.
battles.significance: It nearly broke the young Ottoman state, which fell into eleven years of civil war, and gave Byzantium fifty more years.

battles.name: Battle of Marj Dabiq
battles.outcome: Selim I's guns and musketeers routed the Mamluk cavalry north of Aleppo. Sultan al-Ghawri died on the field.
battles.significance: It opened Syria to the Ottomans; Egypt fell the next year and the Mamluk Sultanate ended.

battles.name: Battle of Haldighati
battles.outcome: Akbar's army under Man Singh fought Maharana Pratap in a narrow mountain pass in Rajasthan. Pratap escaped to the hills.
battles.significance: Mewar was not conquered; Pratap's stand became a lasting symbol of Rajput resistance.
battles.casualties: Uncertain; a few hundred to a few thousand

battles.name: Battle of Karnal
battles.outcome: Nader Shah beat the much larger Mughal army in about three hours, then marched on Delhi and sacked it.
battles.significance: He carried off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor. Mughal power never recovered.

battles.name: Battle of Buxar
battles.outcome: Hector Munro's small Company army beat the joint forces of the Mughal emperor and the Nawabs of Bengal and Awadh on the Ganges.
battles.significance: The Company won the right to collect taxes in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa: the real start of British rule in India.
battles.casualties: About 850 Company killed or wounded; around 2,000 allied dead

battles.name: Battle of Rạch Gầm–Xoài Mút

belligerents.side2: Siam (Rattanakosin Kingdom), with Nguyễn lord forces

battles.outcome: Nguyễn Huệ trapped the Siamese fleet in an ambush on the Mekong river and destroyed it.
battles.significance: It drove the Siamese out of southern Vietnam and made Nguyễn Huệ a national hero.
battles.casualties: Most of the Siamese force lost

links.label: Wikipedia: Battle of Rạch Gầm–Xoài Mút

battles.name: Battle of the Pyramids
battles.outcome: Napoleon's infantry squares broke the Mamluk cavalry charges on the west bank of the Nile, in sight of the pyramids.
battles.significance: It gave France Cairo and Lower Egypt and began the French occupation of Egypt.
battles.casualties: About 300 French killed or wounded; several thousand Mamluk dead

battles.name: Battle of Blaauwberg
battles.outcome: A British army landed north of Cape Town and beat the Dutch defenders on the slopes of the Blaauwberg.
battles.significance: The Cape became a British colony, which shaped the later history of South Africa.
battles.casualties: About 200 British and 350 Dutch killed or wounded

battles.name: Battle of Isly
battles.outcome: Marshal Bugeaud's army routed the Moroccan army near Oujda by the Isly river.
battles.significance: Morocco stopped backing Abd al-Qadir's fight against France in Algeria.

battles.name: Battle of Riachuelo
battles.outcome: The Brazilian river fleet destroyed the Paraguayan navy on the Paraná river near Corrientes.
battles.significance: Paraguay lost its fleet and was cut off from the sea for the rest of the war.
battles.casualties: About 250 Brazilian and over 1,000 Paraguayan killed or wounded

commanders.name: Francisco Manuel Barroso
commanders.wiki: Francisco Manuel Barroso, Baron of Amazonas

battles.name: Battle of Tuyutí
battles.outcome: A Paraguayan surprise attack on the allied camp in the marshes of southern Paraguay failed after hours of fighting.
battles.significance: The bloodiest battle in South American history. Paraguay lost much of its army in a single day.
battles.casualties: About 13,000 Paraguayan and 4,000 allied killed or wounded

commanders.name: Manuel Luís Osório
commanders.wiki: Manuel Luís Osório, Marquis of Erval

battles.name: Battle of Magdala
battles.outcome: A British and Indian army marched across the Ethiopian highlands, beat Tewodros II's army and stormed his mountain fortress.
battles.significance: Tewodros shot himself rather than be taken. The British freed the captives and then left.

commanders.name: Robert Napier
commanders.wiki: Robert Napier, 1st Baron Napier of Magdala

battles.name: Battle of Tacna
battles.outcome: The Chilean army beat the allied army on the Alto de la Alianza plateau above Tacna in the War of the Pacific.
battles.significance: Bolivia left the war, and later lost its coastline. Chile went on to take Lima.
battles.casualties: About 2,100 Chilean and several thousand allied killed or wounded

battles.name: Battle of Maiwand
battles.outcome: Ayub Khan's army beat a British brigade west of Kandahar in the Second Anglo-Afghan War.
battles.significance: One of the worst British defeats in Asia. Malalai of Maiwand became an Afghan heroine.
battles.casualties: About 950 British and Indian dead; perhaps 2,500 Afghan

battles.name: Battle of Manila Bay
battles.outcome: Commodore Dewey's squadron sank the Spanish fleet at anchor off Cavite in a few hours, losing no ships.
battles.significance: The first big battle of the Spanish-American War. It led to American rule of the Philippines.
battles.casualties: 1 American dead (not in combat); about 160 Spanish

battles.name: Battle of Qarqar

belligerents.side2: Coalition of Levantine kings (Damascus, Israel and others)

battles.outcome: Shalmaneser III fought a league of twelve kings by the Orontes river. He claimed a win but did not push on for years.
battles.significance: The first record of Arabs (with camels) in a battle, and the first mention of King Ahab of Israel outside the Bible.

battles.name: Battle of Carchemish

belligerents.side2: Egypt, with the last Assyrian forces

battles.outcome: Crown prince Nebuchadnezzar crushed the army of Pharaoh Necho II at Carchemish on the Euphrates.
battles.significance: It ended Egyptian power in Syria and made Babylon the master of the Near East.

battles.name: Battle of Cunaxa

belligerents.side1: Cyrus the Younger, with Greek mercenaries

battles.outcome: The Greek mercenaries won on their wing, but Cyrus was killed charging at his brother, so his revolt failed.
battles.significance: The stranded 'Ten Thousand' Greeks then marched home, a journey told by Xenophon in the Anabasis.

battles.name: Battle of Jaxartes
battles.outcome: Alexander crossed the Syr Darya river under catapult cover and beat the Scythian horse archers.
battles.significance: It made Alexander's far north-east frontier safe, near today's Khujand in Tajikistan.

battles.name: Battle of Raphia
battles.outcome: Ptolemy IV beat Antiochus III near Gaza in one of the largest battles of the ancient world, with war elephants on both sides.
battles.significance: It kept southern Syria and Palestine in Egyptian hands for almost twenty more years.

battles.name: Battle of Uhud
battles.outcome: Muslim archers left their hill post too early, and a Meccan cavalry charge led by Khalid ibn al-Walid broke Muhammad's army.
battles.significance: A setback for early Islam, but Mecca did not follow it up by taking Medina.
battles.casualties: About 70 Muslims and about 22–37 Meccans killed

battles.name: Second Battle of Dongola
battles.outcome: The Christian Nubian kingdom of Makuria held off an Arab army besieging its capital, Dongola.
battles.significance: It led to the Baqt treaty, which kept Nubia independent and Christian for about 600 years.

battles.name: Battle of Bạch Đằng (938)
battles.outcome: Ngô Quyền planted iron-tipped stakes in the river bed. When the tide went out, the Southern Han fleet was caught and destroyed.
battles.significance: It ended about a thousand years of Chinese rule over northern Vietnam.

battles.name: Battle of Dandanaqan
battles.outcome: Seljuk horsemen beat the larger, thirsty Ghaznavid army in the desert near Merv.
battles.significance: It founded the Seljuk Empire, which went on to rule Iran, Iraq and Anatolia.

battles.name: Capture of Malacca
battles.outcome: Afonso de Albuquerque's fleet stormed the port city after weeks of fighting.
battles.significance: Portugal took control of the Strait of Malacca, the key sea route of the spice trade.

battles.name: Battle of Mactan

belligerents.side2: Spanish expedition of Magellan, with Cebu allies

battles.outcome: Lapulapu's warriors drove off Magellan's landing party, and Magellan was killed in the shallows.
battles.significance: It ended Magellan's own voyage, though his ships went on to finish the first trip around the world.
battles.casualties: Magellan and several of his men killed

battles.name: Battle of Elmina
battles.outcome: Dutch troops landing to take São Jorge da Mina castle were ambushed and routed by the Portuguese and their local allies.
battles.significance: One of the Dutch Republic's worst colonial defeats. Elmina stayed Portuguese until the Dutch took it in 1637.

battles.name: Second Battle of Guararapes
battles.outcome: Luso-Brazilian forces beat the Dutch again on the Guararapes hills south of Recife.
battles.significance: It broke Dutch power in north-east Brazil, which fell in 1654. Brazil marks it as the birth of its army.

battles.name: Battle of Maipú
battles.outcome: José de San Martín's army destroyed the royalist army on the plain near Santiago.
battles.significance: It secured Chile's independence from Spain.

battles.name: Battle of Carabobo
battles.outcome: Simón Bolívar's army, helped by the British Legion, routed the royalists on the plain of Carabobo.
battles.significance: It won the independence of Venezuela.

battles.name: Battle of Megiddo
battles.outcome: Canaanite coalition besieged and defeated at Megiddo.
battles.significance: The earliest battle recorded with reliable detail, and the origin of the name 'Armageddon' (Har Megiddo).

links.label: Wikipedia: Battle of Megiddo (15th c. BC)

battles.name: Battle of Kadesh
battles.outcome: Tactical draw; neither side took Kadesh, and both claimed victory.
battles.significance: Probably the largest chariot battle ever fought, and one of the best-recorded battles of the ancient world. About sixteen years later the two powers signed the earliest peace treaty whose text survives (c. 1259 BCE).

battles.name: Battle of Marathon
battles.outcome: Persian invasion repelled.
battles.significance: A heavily outnumbered Greek force defeated Persia, preserving Greek independence and inspiring the legend of the marathon run.

battles.name: Battle of Salamis
battles.outcome: Persian fleet crushed in the straits.
battles.significance: A decisive naval victory that broke Persia's invasion of Greece and shifted the balance of the Greco-Persian Wars.

battles.name: Battle of Thermopylae
battles.outcome: Greek rearguard annihilated after holding the pass for days.
battles.significance: The famous last stand of 300 Spartans and their allies became the enduring symbol of courage against overwhelming odds.

battles.name: Battle of Plataea
battles.outcome: The Persian land army in Greece was destroyed.
battles.significance: The decisive land battle that ended the Persian invasion of Greece for good.
battles.casualties: Thousands Greek; tens of thousands Persian

battles.name: Battle of Issus
battles.outcome: Darius fled the field, abandoning his family.
battles.significance: Alexander's first direct victory over Darius, opening the Levant and Egypt to conquest.

battles.name: Battle of Gaugamela
battles.outcome: Persian army shattered; Darius fled.
battles.significance: Alexander's decisive victory ended the Achaemenid Empire and opened the East to Hellenistic civilization.

battles.name: Battle of the Hydaspes
battles.outcome: Porus defeated despite war elephants; Alexander's eastward limit.
battles.significance: Alexander's last great battle, at the edge of the known world, against war elephants in India.

battles.name: Battle of Cannae
battles.outcome: A Roman army of ~80,000 was encircled and destroyed.
battles.significance: Hannibal's double-envelopment is still taught as the perfect tactical battle, though Rome would ultimately win the war.

battles.name: Battle of Zama
battles.outcome: Hannibal defeated; Second Punic War ended.
battles.significance: Rome's victory ended Carthage as a great power and set Rome on the path to Mediterranean dominance.

battles.name: Battle of Gaixia
battles.outcome: Xiang Yu's army was surrounded and broke up; he fled and killed himself at the Wu River.
battles.significance: Ended the Chu–Han Contention. Liu Bang became the first emperor of the Han dynasty, which ruled China for four centuries.

battles.name: Siege of Carthage
battles.outcome: The walls were breached and the city taken street by street over six days. Carthage was burned and its survivors sold into slavery.
battles.significance: The end of Carthage as a state, and of any rival to Rome in the western Mediterranean. Rome would face no serious competitor there for three hundred years. The story that the Romans sowed the ground with salt is a nineteenth-century invention.
battles.casualties: Perhaps 150,000 Carthaginians dead; some 50,000 survivors enslaved

battles.name: Battle of Carrhae
battles.outcome: A Roman army destroyed by horse archers; Crassus killed.
battles.significance: One of Rome's worst defeats, exposing the limits of the legion against mobile cavalry.

battles.name: Siege of Alesia
battles.outcome: Vercingetorix surrendered; Gaul was subdued.
battles.significance: Caesar's double-siege masterpiece completed the Roman conquest of Gaul.

battles.name: Battle of Pharsalus
battles.outcome: Pompey routed; he fled to Egypt and was killed.
battles.significance: Caesar's victory in Rome's civil war cleared his path to dictatorship and the end of the Republic.

battles.name: Battle of Actium
battles.outcome: Antony and Cleopatra's fleet defeated.
battles.significance: The naval victory made Octavian sole master of Rome, leading to the founding of the Roman Empire.

battles.name: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
battles.outcome: Three Roman legions ambushed and destroyed.
battles.significance: The disaster halted Roman expansion east of the Rhine and shaped the boundary between Roman and Germanic Europe.

links.label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest

battles.name: Battle of Red Cliffs
battles.outcome: Cao Cao's fleet burned; his southern advance stopped.
battles.significance: A pivotal battle of China's Three Kingdoms period that prevented unification under Cao Cao and is immortalised in legend.

battles.name: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
battles.outcome: Maxentius drowned in the Tiber; Constantine took Rome.
battles.significance: Led Constantine to embrace Christianity, changing the religious course of the Roman Empire and Europe.

links.label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Milvian Bridge

battles.name: Battle of Adrianople
battles.outcome: Emperor Valens killed and his army destroyed.
battles.significance: A catastrophic Roman defeat often seen as a milestone in the decline of the Western Roman Empire.

battles.name: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
battles.outcome: Attila's westward advance was checked.
battles.significance: Halted Attila the Hun's invasion of Gaul, one of the last great victories of the Western Roman Empire.

links.label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains

battles.name: Battle of the Yarmouk
battles.outcome: Byzantine army destroyed; Levant lost to the Caliphate.
battles.significance: One of history's most decisive battles, it ended Byzantine rule in Syria and fuelled the early Islamic conquests.

battles.name: Battle of Tours
battles.outcome: Umayyad advance into Western Europe halted.
battles.significance: Often cited as the battle that checked Muslim expansion into Western Europe and secured the rise of the Frankish kingdom.

battles.name: Battle of Talas

belligerents.side1: Abbasid Caliphate, with Tibetan and (late) Karluk allies

battles.outcome: After five days of fighting the Karluk mercenaries in the Tang army changed sides, and Gao Xianzhi's army broke. Only a few thousand of his men got home.
battles.significance: The only battle ever fought between the Arab caliphate and Tang China. It marked the western limit of Tang power in Central Asia. The story that Chinese prisoners taught Samarkand to make paper is old but unproven. The exact battlefield is not known; the pin is in the upper Talas valley, where Arabic sources place it.
battles.casualties: Tang losses very heavy (Chinese sources: most of an army of perhaps 30,000); Abbasid losses unknown

battles.name: Battle of Lechfeld
battles.outcome: Otto I's German army routed a large Hungarian raiding force near Augsburg.
battles.significance: Ended the Hungarian raids on Western Europe. It boosted Otto I, who was crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 962.

battles.name: Battle of Clontarf

belligerents.side1: Kingdom of Munster and allies (Brian Boru)
belligerents.side2: Leinster and the Norse of Dublin and the Isles

battles.outcome: Brian Boru's army won, but Brian himself was killed in his tent during the battle.
battles.significance: Broke the power of the Norse–Leinster alliance. It is one of the best-remembered battles in Irish history.

battles.name: Battle of Hastings
battles.outcome: King Harold killed; England conquered.
battles.significance: The Norman conquest transformed England's language, law and aristocracy — one of the most consequential battles in British history.

battles.name: Battle of Stamford Bridge
battles.outcome: The Norwegian invasion was crushed; Hardrada killed.
battles.significance: Ended the Viking Age in England — days before Harold marched south to meet William at Hastings.

battles.name: Battle of Manzikert
battles.outcome: Byzantine emperor captured; Anatolia opened to the Turks.
battles.significance: A catastrophe for Byzantium that began the Turkification of Anatolia and helped spark the Crusades.

battles.name: Battle of Hattin
battles.outcome: Crusader army destroyed; Jerusalem soon fell.
battles.significance: Saladin's victory broke the Crusader states and triggered the Third Crusade.
battles.casualties: Most of the ~20,000 Crusader army killed or captured

battles.name: Battle of Yehuling (Badger Mouth)
battles.outcome: The Jin field army was destroyed; northern China lay open.
battles.significance: Genghis Khan’s first great victory over the Jin, and the beginning of the Mongol conquest of northern China.
battles.casualties: Jin losses in the hundreds of thousands, by Chinese accounts

battles.name: Siege of Samarkand
battles.outcome: Samarkand fell in days; the Khwarazmian Empire collapsed within two years.
battles.significance: The campaign that carried the Mongols into Persia and the Middle East, begun as revenge for murdered envoys.
battles.casualties: The garrison massacred; craftsmen deported east

battles.name: Battle of the Kalka River
battles.outcome: A combined Rus’ army destroyed; the Mongols then withdrew east for fourteen years.
battles.significance: Europe’s first meeting with the Mongols — a reconnaissance in force that was not understood as a warning.
battles.casualties: Around nine tenths of the Rus’ army; six princes killed

links.label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Kalka River

battles.name: Battle of Kirina
battles.outcome: The Sosso army was broken and Sumanguru disappeared from the record. Sundiata was proclaimed mansa, and the Mali Empire was founded.
battles.significance: The founding battle of the Mali Empire, whose gold would later mint much of Europe's coinage. It survives chiefly through the oral Epic of Sundiata, so the date is approximate and the battlefield's location traditional rather than proven.

battles.name: Battle of Legnica

belligerents.side2: Poland, Moravia and the military orders

battles.outcome: The Polish army destroyed two days before Mohi; central Europe lay open.
battles.significance: The western edge of the conquest. The Mongols turned back the next year on the death of the Great Khan, not through defeat.
battles.casualties: Most of the Polish force; Duke Henry II killed

battles.name: Battle of Ain Jalut
battles.outcome: The first strategic defeat the Mongols could not reverse; the advance west stopped here for good.
battles.significance: The limit of the empire Genghis began — and the reason Egypt and North Africa were never taken.
battles.casualties: The Mongol force largely destroyed; Kitbuqa executed

battles.name: Battle of Yamen
battles.outcome: The Song fleet destroyed; the child emperor drowned. China united under Mongol rule.
battles.significance: The conquest Genghis began in 1211 completed by his grandson Kublai, sixty-eight years later.
battles.casualties: Reportedly over 100,000 Song dead, many by drowning

battles.name: Battle of Bannockburn
battles.outcome: A larger English army routed.
battles.significance: Secured Scottish independence for a generation and became a national symbol.

battles.name: Battle of Crécy
battles.outcome: French cavalry shattered by English longbows.
battles.significance: An early, decisive English victory of the Hundred Years' War that announced the dominance of the longbow.

battles.name: Battle of Grunwald (Tannenberg)
battles.outcome: The Teutonic Order's army destroyed.
battles.significance: One of the largest battles of medieval Europe; it broke the power of the Teutonic Knights.

battles.name: Battle of Agincourt
battles.outcome: French nobility slaughtered by English longbowmen in the mud.
battles.significance: A stunning underdog victory in the Hundred Years' War that showcased the power of the longbow over armoured knights.

battles.name: Fall of Constantinople
battles.outcome: The city fell; the Byzantine Empire ended.
battles.significance: Gunpowder cannon breached the great walls, ending the Roman/Byzantine Empire after ~1,500 years and marking a turning point into the early modern era.

battles.name: Battle of Towton
battles.outcome: Fought in a snowstorm; the Lancastrian army broke and many drowned in the Cock Beck.
battles.significance: Often called the largest and bloodiest battle ever fought on English soil. It secured the throne for Edward IV.

battles.name: Battle of Bosworth Field
battles.outcome: Richard III killed; Henry VII crowned.
battles.significance: The last decisive battle of the Wars of the Roses, beginning the Tudor dynasty.

battles.name: La Noche Triste
battles.outcome: Cortés driven out of Tenochtitlan overnight with heavy losses.
battles.significance: The night the conquest nearly failed. The Spanish returned a year later with smallpox ahead of them.
battles.casualties: Perhaps two thirds of the Spanish force and most of their allies

battles.name: Fall of Tenochtitlan
battles.outcome: The Aztec capital fell after a brutal siege.
battles.significance: Ended the Aztec Empire and began Spanish rule in Mexico — a turning point of the Columbian era.
battles.casualties: Tens of thousands (mostly Aztec, incl. disease)

battles.name: Battle of Mohács
battles.outcome: The Hungarian king and army destroyed.
battles.significance: Opened central Europe to Ottoman expansion and ended independent medieval Hungary.

battles.name: First Battle of Panipat
battles.outcome: Lodi killed; Babur took Delhi.
battles.significance: Founded the Mughal Empire in India, partly through early use of gunpowder artillery.

battles.name: Battle of Cajamarca
battles.outcome: Atahualpa seized in the square by fewer than 200 men; the Inca state decapitated in an afternoon.
battles.significance: An empire of millions taken by ambush — smallpox and a war of succession had come first.
battles.casualties: Thousands of Inca killed; almost no Spanish losses

battles.name: Battle of Lepanto
battles.outcome: Ottoman galley fleet destroyed.
battles.significance: The last great galley battle halted Ottoman naval dominance in the Mediterranean and boosted European morale.

battles.name: Battle of Alcácer Quibir

belligerents.side2: Portugal and the deposed claimant Abu Abdallah

battles.outcome: The Portuguese army was surrounded and destroyed in an afternoon. King Sebastian was killed, the claimant drowned in the river, and the victorious sultan died of illness during the battle itself.
battles.significance: Three kings died in a single day, which is why it is also called the Battle of the Three Kings. Portugal lost its king, its nobility and its army, and within two years its independence to Spain. Morocco stayed free of European rule for another three centuries.
battles.casualties: Around 8,000 Portuguese dead and 15,000 taken prisoner

commanders.name: Abd al-Malik I
commanders.wiki: Abu Marwan Abd al-Malik I Saadi

battles.name: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
battles.outcome: The decisive fight was off Gravelines, Flanders. Fireships broke the Armada's crescent; it fled north round Scotland and Ireland and many ships were wrecked on the way home.
battles.significance: A pivotal moment that checked Spanish power and bolstered England as a naval nation.

commanders.name: Duke of Medina Sidonia
commanders.wiki: Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, 7th Duke of Medina Sidonia

battles.name: Battle of Tondibi
battles.outcome: A few thousand Moroccans with arquebuses and cannon broke a Songhai army many times their size. Gao fell within days, Timbuktu within weeks.
battles.significance: Gunpowder ended the age of the great West African empires. Timbuktu's scholars were arrested and deported, its libraries scattered, and the Niger trade never took its old shape again.
battles.casualties: Thousands of Songhai dead; Moroccan losses light

battles.name: Battle of Sekigahara
battles.outcome: Several Western Army lords switched sides mid-battle, and the Western Army collapsed.
battles.significance: Made Tokugawa Ieyasu master of Japan. His shogunate ruled for over 250 years, until 1868.

battles.name: Battle of Breitenfeld

belligerents.side2: Holy Roman Empire and Catholic League

battles.outcome: Gustavus Adolphus's flexible Swedish army smashed Tilly's veteran imperial army near Leipzig.
battles.significance: The first great Protestant victory of the Thirty Years' War. It showed the power of new, mobile tactics.

battles.name: Battle of Rocroi
battles.outcome: The young Duke of Enghien broke a Spanish army besieging the French town of Rocroi.
battles.significance: Marked the end of Spain's famous tercio infantry as Europe's best, and the rise of French military power.
battles.casualties: About 4,000 French and 15,000 Spanish (killed, wounded or captured)

battles.name: Battle of Naseby
battles.outcome: The main Royalist army destroyed.
battles.significance: The decisive battle of the English Civil War, sealing the defeat of Charles I.

commanders.name: Thomas Fairfax
commanders.wiki: Thomas Fairfax, 3rd Lord Fairfax of Cameron

battles.name: Battle of Vienna

belligerents.side1: Holy Roman Empire & Poland (Jan III Sobieski)

battles.outcome: The Ottoman siege of Vienna was broken by a massive cavalry charge.
battles.significance: Marked the high-water mark of Ottoman expansion in Europe and the start of their long retreat.

battles.name: Battle of Blenheim
battles.outcome: A French army destroyed; Vienna saved.
battles.significance: A landmark victory in the War of the Spanish Succession that ended French dominance of Western Europe.

battles.name: Battle of Poltava
battles.outcome: Swedish army crushed.
battles.significance: Ended Sweden's status as a great power and announced Russia's rise in the Great Northern War.

battles.name: Battle of Culloden
battles.outcome: The Jacobite rising crushed in under an hour.
battles.significance: The last pitched battle on British soil; it ended the Jacobite cause and the clan system.

battles.name: Battle of Plassey
battles.outcome: Bengal fell under Company control.
battles.significance: A decisive (and largely bribery-won) victory that began British political dominance over India.

battles.name: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
battles.outcome: Quebec fell; both commanders died.
battles.significance: Decided the fate of New France and set North America on a British path.

links.label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Plains of Abraham

battles.name: Battles of Saratoga
battles.outcome: A British army surrendered.
battles.significance: The turning point of the American Revolution — the victory brought France into the war on the American side.

battles.name: Siege of Yorktown
battles.outcome: Cornwallis surrendered ~8,000 men.
battles.significance: The decisive siege that effectively ended the American Revolutionary War and secured U.S. independence.

commanders.name: Comte de Rochambeau
commanders.wiki: Jean-Baptiste Donatien de Vimeur, comte de Rochambeau

battles.name: Battle of Valmy
battles.outcome: Prussian advance on Paris halted by an artillery duel.
battles.significance: A morale-defining victory that saved the French Revolution; the Republic was declared the next day.

commanders.name: Duke of Brunswick
commanders.wiki: Charles William Ferdinand, Duke of Brunswick

battles.name: Battle of the Nile
battles.outcome: Eleven of the thirteen French ships of the line were captured or destroyed. The flagship L'Orient blew up at ten at night with her captain's young son aboard.
battles.significance: Nelson attacked at dusk and sent half his fleet between the French line and the shore, where the enemy had not run out their landward guns. It stranded Bonaparte's army in Egypt and made the Mediterranean a British sea.
battles.casualties: Around 5,000 French dead, wounded or captured; 218 British dead

battles.name: Battle of Austerlitz
battles.outcome: The allied army was split and routed.
battles.significance: Napoleon's tactical masterpiece — the 'Battle of the Three Emperors' shattered the Third Coalition.

battles.name: Battle of Trafalgar
battles.outcome: Franco-Spanish fleet destroyed; Nelson killed.
battles.significance: Confirmed British naval supremacy for over a century and ended Napoleon's hopes of invading Britain.

battles.name: Battle of Jena–Auerstedt
battles.outcome: The Prussian army shattered in a single day.
battles.significance: Demonstrated French military supremacy and brought Prussia to its knees.

commanders.name: Duke of Brunswick
commanders.wiki: Charles William Ferdinand, Duke of Brunswick

battles.name: Battle of Borodino
battles.outcome: Russians withdrew; Moscow soon abandoned.
battles.significance: The bloodiest single day of the Napoleonic Wars; a Pyrrhic victory before the catastrophic French retreat from Russia.

battles.name: Battle of Leipzig
battles.outcome: Napoleon decisively defeated and driven out of Germany.
battles.significance: The 'Battle of Nations' was the largest battle in Europe before WWI and broke Napoleon's grip on the continent.

battles.name: Battle of Waterloo
battles.outcome: Napoleon's final defeat; he abdicated days later.
battles.significance: Ended the Napoleonic Wars and a quarter-century of conflict, ushering in a century of relative European peace.

battles.name: Battle of Ayacucho
battles.outcome: Antonio José de Sucre's army defeated the Viceroy, who was captured and signed a surrender.
battles.significance: The last major battle of the Spanish American wars of independence. It ended Spanish rule in South America.

commanders.name: José de la Serna
commanders.wiki: José de la Serna e Hinojosa

battles.name: Battle of Navarino
battles.outcome: The allied squadrons sailed into Navarino Bay to enforce a truce. Firing broke out, and in four hours about three-quarters of the Ottoman–Egyptian fleet was sunk, burnt or wrecked. The allies lost no ships.
battles.significance: The last great sea battle fought wholly by sailing ships. It ended Ottoman hopes of crushing the Greek revolt and led directly to Greek independence.
battles.casualties: About 180 allied dead; Ottoman–Egyptian dead in the thousands

battles.name: Pinjarra Massacre

belligerents.side1: British colonial force of Western Australia

battles.outcome: A dawn attack on a Binjareb camp on the Murray River, with the party divided to cut off retreat across the water.
battles.significance: One of the best-documented actions of the Australian Frontier Wars, and a case where the name itself is contested: the colonists called it the Battle of Pinjarra, and most historians and the Noongar community now call it a massacre.
battles.casualties: Between 15 and 80 Binjareb dead, including women and children; one colonial soldier killed

battles.name: Battle of the Alamo
battles.outcome: The mission stormed after a thirteen-day siege; nearly all defenders killed.
battles.significance: A tactical defeat that became the rallying cry of Texan independence six weeks later at San Jacinto.
battles.casualties: Around 200 Texian defenders; several hundred Mexican soldiers

battles.name: Battle of Blood River
battles.outcome: Around 470 trekkers in a wagon laager, with cannon and muskets, held off a Zulu army attacking across open ground. The Ncome river is said to have run red.
battles.significance: A firepower massacre that became the founding myth of Afrikaner nationalism, kept as a public holiday for a century and a half. Since 1995 the same date has been South Africa's Day of Reconciliation.
battles.casualties: Around 3,000 Zulu dead; three Voortrekkers wounded and none killed

battles.name: Siege of Ruapekapeka

belligerents.side2: Ngāpuhi under Te Ruki Kawiti and Hōne Heke

battles.victor: Inconclusive — the pā was entered only after it was abandoned
battles.outcome: The heaviest bombardment yet seen in New Zealand failed to drive out the garrison, who slipped away into the bush and left the British an empty fortress.
battles.significance: Kawiti built Ruapekapeka specifically to absorb artillery: earth bunkers, communication trenches and firing pits, with the palisade as bait rather than defence. Military engineers studied the design, which anticipated the trench systems of 1916 by seventy years.
battles.casualties: Around 12 British dead; Māori losses similar

battles.name: Battle of Balaclava
battles.outcome: Famous for the doomed Charge of the Light Brigade.
battles.significance: A Crimean War battle remembered for a heroic but disastrous cavalry charge.

battles.name: Eureka Stockade
battles.victor: Colonial victory — but the miners' demands were granted within a year
battles.outcome: Troops and police stormed the miners' timber stockade at dawn and took it in about fifteen minutes. Every miner later put on trial was acquitted by a Melbourne jury.
battles.significance: Australia's only armed rebellion. The hated licence fee was abolished, the miners got the vote, and the Southern Cross flag raised over the stockade became a national symbol claimed ever since by almost everyone.

battles.name: Battle of Solferino
battles.outcome: A huge, confused battle with three emperors and kings commanding in person. Austria fell back.
battles.significance: A key step toward Italian unification. The suffering of the wounded inspired Henry Dunant to found the Red Cross.
battles.casualties: About 40,000 killed and wounded on both sides

battles.name: Battle of Antietam
battles.outcome: Lee's invasion of the North turned back.
battles.significance: The bloodiest single day in American history; it gave Lincoln the moment to issue the Emancipation Proclamation.

battles.name: Battle of Gettysburg
battles.outcome: Lee's second invasion of the North decisively repelled.
battles.significance: The turning point of the American Civil War and its bloodiest battle, immortalised by Lincoln's Gettysburg Address.

battles.name: Battle of Gate Pā
battles.outcome: A day-long bombardment appeared to flatten the pā, but the defenders were safe in bunkers. The British assault column walked into crossfire in the trenches and was thrown back with most of its officers down.
battles.significance: Remembered as much for the night that followed as for the defeat: the defenders gave water to wounded British soldiers lying in the ruins. The rules of conduct written before the battle by Hēnare Taratoa are still quoted in New Zealand.
battles.casualties: 31 British dead and 80 wounded; around 25 Māori dead

battles.name: Battle of Ōrākau
battles.outcome: Around 300 defenders, out of water and reduced to firing wooden bullets, refused terms and broke out through the British lines in broad daylight. Many were cut down in the retreat.
battles.significance: Rewi Maniapoto's answer to the call to surrender — Ka whawhai tonu mātou, ake, ake, ake! We will fight on for ever — became the most quoted sentence in New Zealand history. The battle ended the invasion of the Waikato.

battles.name: Battle of Königgrätz
battles.outcome: Austria decisively beaten.
battles.significance: Settled the leadership of Germany in Prussia's favour, a key step toward German unification.

battles.name: Battle of Sedan
battles.outcome: Napoleon III captured with his army.
battles.significance: The decisive battle of the Franco-Prussian War; it toppled the French Empire and led to German unification.

battles.name: Battle of the Little Bighorn
battles.outcome: Custer and his command annihilated.
battles.significance: A famous Native American victory ('Custer's Last Stand') during the Great Sioux War.

links.label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Little Bighorn

battles.name: Battle of Isandlwana
battles.outcome: A British camp of some 1,800 was enveloped by the Zulu horns-of-the-buffalo formation and destroyed almost to the last man, under a partial solar eclipse.
battles.significance: The heaviest defeat a modern European army ever suffered at the hands of a force armed mainly with spears. It stunned Victorian Britain and is still taught as the classic lesson in underestimating an opponent.
battles.casualties: Around 1,300 British and allied dead; perhaps 1,000 to 2,000 Zulu

battles.name: Battle of Rorke's Drift
battles.outcome: About 150 men, a third of them sick, held a mission station behind mealie bags and biscuit boxes through a night of assaults by three to four thousand Zulu.
battles.significance: Eleven Victoria Crosses were awarded, seven of them to the 24th Foot — the most ever won by one regiment in a single action. They were given partly so the newspapers would have something creditable to print alongside Isandlwana, fought the same day a few miles away.

battles.name: Battle of Adwa
battles.outcome: The Italian invasion army defeated.
battles.significance: A landmark victory of an African state over a European colonial power, securing Ethiopian independence.

battles.name: Battle of Omdurman
battles.outcome: Maxim guns, artillery and Nile gunboats destroyed a Mahdist army of some 50,000 in about five hours of largely one-sided fire.
battles.significance: The plainest demonstration of what the machine gun had done to war: 47 dead on one side, around 12,000 on the other. A young Winston Churchill rode in the cavalry charge and wrote the account that made his name.

battles.name: Battle of Tsushima
battles.outcome: The Russian Baltic Fleet annihilated.
battles.significance: A crushing naval victory that ended the Russo-Japanese War and announced Japan as a great power.

battles.name: Battle of Mukden
battles.outcome: After three weeks of fighting on a front about 150 km long, the Russian armies fell back north and Mukden (Shenyang) was taken.
battles.significance: The largest land battle fought anywhere before the First World War, with over half a million men. With Tsushima ten weeks later, it ended the Russo-Japanese War.
battles.casualties: About 75,000 Japanese; about 90,000 Russian, including some 20,000 captured

battles.name: Battle of Bita Paka
battles.outcome: A naval landing party fought inland through the plantations to take the German wireless station. The colony surrendered a week later.
battles.significance: Australia's first action of the First World War and its first battle as a federated nation, fought seven months before Gallipoli. The station was one of the wireless posts directing German raiders across the Pacific.
battles.casualties: 6 Australian dead; around 30 German and Melanesian dead

battles.name: First Battle of the Marne
battles.outcome: The German advance on Paris was halted and reversed.
battles.significance: Ended Germany's hopes of a quick victory and began the long stalemate of trench warfare.

links.label: Wikipedia: First Battle of the Marne

battles.name: Battle of Tannenberg
battles.outcome: The Russian Second Army was surrounded in the forests and lakes of East Prussia and almost wiped out. Its commander, Samsonov, shot himself.
battles.significance: Made Hindenburg and Ludendorff national heroes. It was fought near Allenstein, but named after Tannenberg, about 30 km away, to answer the German defeat there in 1410 (Grunwald).
battles.casualties: About 12,000 German; about 78,000 Russian killed or wounded and some 92,000 captured

battles.name: Gallipoli Campaign
battles.outcome: Allied landings failed; eventual withdrawal.
battles.significance: A costly Allied failure that became a defining national moment for Australia, New Zealand and Turkey.

battles.name: Battle of Jutland
battles.outcome: Both fleets withdrew; British blockade held.
battles.significance: The largest naval battle of WWI; though tactically inconclusive, it kept the German fleet bottled up for the rest of the war.

battles.name: Battle of the Somme
battles.outcome: Small territorial gains at staggering cost.
battles.significance: One of the bloodiest battles in history; its first day remains the deadliest in British Army history.

battles.name: Battle of Verdun
battles.outcome: German offensive ground to a halt after months.
battles.significance: The longest battle of WWI and a symbol of the war's industrial-scale attrition ('They shall not pass').

battles.name: Battle of Passchendaele (Third Ypres)
battles.victor: Inconclusive; the Allies took the ridge
battles.outcome: Fifteen weeks of attacks in heavy rain on shell-churned clay gained about 8 km. Canadian troops finally took the ruined village of Passchendaele on 6 November.
battles.significance: The name became a byword for the mud and waste of the Western Front. The ridge it cost so much to take was given up within months, in the German spring offensive of 1918.
battles.casualties: Estimates differ widely: roughly 250,000 on each side

battles.name: Battle of Amiens

belligerents.side1: British Empire and France (Rawlinson; Australian and Canadian corps)

battles.outcome: A surprise attack in fog, with over 500 tanks and aircraft, broke through on a 20 km front and advanced about 11 km on the first day.
battles.significance: The opening of the Hundred Days Offensive that ended the war three months later. Ludendorff called 8 August 'the black day of the German Army'.
battles.casualties: About 44,000 Allied; about 75,000 German, many of them prisoners

battles.name: Battle of Britain
battles.outcome: The planned German invasion of Britain was called off.
battles.significance: The first major campaign fought entirely in the air; the RAF's defence denied Germany the skies over Britain.

battles.name: Battle of Dunkirk
battles.outcome: Germany took Dunkirk, but over 338,000 Allied troops escaped by sea in Operation Dynamo.
battles.significance: The 'miracle of Dunkirk' saved the British Army to fight on after the fall of France.
battles.casualties: Tens of thousands; about 35,000 French troops captured

battles.name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
battles.outcome: The U.S. Pacific Fleet battleships crippled in a surprise attack.
battles.significance: Brought the United States into World War II.

battles.name: Battle of Moscow
battles.outcome: The German drive on Moscow stalled in winter, and a Soviet counter-attack pushed it back.
battles.significance: The first major German defeat of World War II on land. It ended Hitler's hope of a quick win against the Soviet Union.
battles.casualties: Very heavy: roughly 1 million Soviet and 500,000+ German casualties

battles.name: Battle of the Coral Sea
battles.outcome: The invasion convoy bound for Port Moresby turned back. The Americans lost the carrier Lexington, the Japanese lost Shōhō and had Shōkaku crippled and Zuikaku's air groups gutted.
battles.significance: The first naval battle in history in which the opposing fleets never sighted one another — everything was done by aircraft. The two Japanese carriers knocked out here were missing from Midway a month later.
battles.casualties: Around 650 Allied dead; around 950 Japanese dead

links.label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Coral Sea

battles.name: Second Battle of El Alamein
battles.outcome: Axis forces driven into retreat across North Africa.
battles.significance: A major turning point in the North African campaign — 'the end of the beginning' for the Allies.

links.label: Wikipedia: Second Battle of El Alamein

commanders.name: Bernard Montgomery
commanders.wiki: Bernard Montgomery, 1st Viscount Montgomery of Alamein

battles.name: Guadalcanal Campaign
battles.outcome: Six months of jungle fighting, night surface actions and carrier battles around one airstrip ended with Japan evacuating the island by destroyer.
battles.significance: The first Allied offensive of the Pacific war and its turning point — after Guadalcanal Japan never mounted another strategic advance. So many ships went down in the strait to the north that it is still called Ironbottom Sound.
battles.casualties: Around 7,100 Allied dead; around 31,000 Japanese dead

battles.name: Kokoda Track Campaign
battles.outcome: Japanese forces pushed within about 50 km of Port Moresby before starvation and Australian counterattacks drove them back over the Owen Stanley Range.
battles.significance: The closest a Japanese army came to Australia, fought in mud on a single-file mountain track where a stretcher case took eight men and several days. For Australians it carries the weight Gallipoli does — a story of endurance rather than of victory.
battles.casualties: Around 625 Australian dead; some 6,000 Japanese dead from all causes

battles.name: Battle of Midway
battles.outcome: Four Japanese aircraft carriers sunk.
battles.significance: The decisive turning point of the Pacific War, ending Japanese naval expansion six months after Pearl Harbor.

battles.name: Battle of Milne Bay
battles.outcome: A Japanese amphibious landing was contained in the coconut plantations, beaten back, and finally evacuated by sea at night.
battles.significance: The first time in the war that a Japanese landing force was defeated outright on land. Field Marshal Slim later wrote that Milne Bay was where the myth of Japanese invincibility was broken.
battles.casualties: Around 170 Allied dead; around 750 Japanese dead

battles.name: Battle of Stalingrad
battles.outcome: An entire German army encircled and destroyed.
battles.significance: The bloodiest battle in history and the decisive turning point of WWII's Eastern Front.

battles.name: Battle of Kursk
battles.outcome: The last major German offensive in the East failed.
battles.significance: The largest tank battle in history; after Kursk the strategic initiative on the Eastern Front passed permanently to the USSR.

battles.name: Battle of the Bulge
battles.outcome: Germany's last major western offensive failed.
battles.significance: The costliest single battle for U.S. forces in WWII; it exhausted Germany's reserves in the west.

battles.name: D-Day (Normandy Landings)
battles.outcome: Allied armies established a foothold in occupied France.
battles.significance: The largest seaborne invasion in history opened the Western Front and began the liberation of Western Europe.
battles.casualties: ~10,000 Allied casualties on the first day

commanders.name: Bernard Montgomery
commanders.wiki: Bernard Montgomery, 1st Viscount Montgomery of Alamein

battles.name: Battle of Leyte Gulf
battles.outcome: The Japanese navy was crippled as a fighting force.
battles.significance: Generally considered the largest naval battle in history; it sealed Japan's naval defeat.

battles.name: Falaise Pocket

belligerents.side1: Allies (Montgomery & Bradley; Canadian, Polish, British and US troops)

battles.outcome: Two German armies were trapped between Falaise and Chambois. Polish troops on Hill 262 held the last gap until it closed on 21 August.
battles.significance: The end of the Battle of Normandy. The German army in the west lost most of its equipment, and Paris was free four days later.
battles.casualties: About 10,000 German dead and 40,000–50,000 captured; Allied losses far lighter

battles.name: Battle of Berlin
battles.outcome: Berlin captured; Hitler died; Germany surrendered.
battles.significance: The final major battle in Europe, ending the Third Reich and the Second World War on the continent.

battles.name: Battle of Iwo Jima
battles.outcome: Five weeks of fighting against defenders dug into tunnels under the volcanic island. Almost the whole garrison died; only about 216 were taken prisoner.
battles.significance: The only major US Marine battle of the war in which American casualties (dead and wounded) outnumbered the Japanese. The photograph of the flag raised on Mount Suribachi on 23 February became one of the most famous images of the war.
battles.casualties: About 6,800 American dead (26,000 casualties); about 18,000 Japanese dead

battles.name: Battle of Okinawa
battles.outcome: After 82 days of fighting, US forces took the island; Japanese commanders died by suicide at the end.
battles.significance: The largest amphibious assault of the Pacific War, and one of its bloodiest. It shaped the decision to use the atomic bombs.
battles.casualties: About 50,000 Allied casualties, 77,000–110,000 Japanese soldiers and many thousands of civilians killed

battles.name: Battle of Chosin Reservoir
battles.victor: Chinese strategic victory; the encircled force broke out
battles.outcome: Surrounded by ten divisions at thirty degrees below freezing, the Marines fought seventy-eight miles to the sea and took their wounded and their dead with them.
battles.significance: China had entered the war, and the hope of a quick reunification died in the snow. The front settled near where it had started, and is still there.
battles.casualties: About 17,800 UN casualties, many from frostbite; Chinese losses far higher

battles.name: Battle of Inchon
battles.outcome: A daring amphibious landing turned the Korean War.
battles.significance: Reversed the course of the Korean War almost overnight by cutting off North Korean forces.

battles.name: The Pusan Perimeter

belligerents.side1: United Nations Command and South Korea

battles.outcome: Six weeks defending the last south-eastern corner of the peninsula, until Inchon cut the attackers off from behind.
battles.significance: The invasion came within a hundred miles of taking the whole country. Everything after Korea in the Cold War was shaped by the fact that it did not.
battles.casualties: Tens of thousands on both sides; North Korean losses the heavier

battles.name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
battles.outcome: The French garrison besieged and forced to surrender.
battles.significance: Ended French colonial rule in Indochina and led to the division of Vietnam.

links.label: Wikipedia: Battle of Dien Bien Phu

battles.name: The Suez Crisis
battles.outcome: The canal zone was taken and then given straight back under American and Soviet pressure, with the pound under threat.
battles.significance: The moment Britain discovered it could no longer act as a great power without Washington’s consent. Eden resigned; the empire’s unwinding accelerated.
battles.casualties: Around 3,000 Egyptian and some 200 allied dead

battles.name: Battle of Ia Drang
battles.outcome: Two savage engagements days apart — a held landing zone at X-Ray, then an ambushed column at Albany.
battles.significance: The first full battle between American regulars and the North Vietnamese Army, and the first fought from helicopters. Each side came away believing it could beat the other, which is why the war ran another decade.
battles.casualties: About 234 Americans killed; North Vietnamese losses far higher and never reliably counted

battles.name: The Six-Day War
battles.outcome: The Egyptian air force destroyed on the ground in three hours; Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan taken in under a week.
battles.significance: Redrew the map of the Middle East and created the occupations that define its politics still. Six days, and the argument has run for six decades.
battles.casualties: Around 800 Israeli dead; Arab losses estimated near 20,000

battles.name: Battle of Huế

belligerents.side1: South Vietnam and the United States
belligerents.side2: North Vietnam and the Viet Cong

battles.outcome: A month of house-to-house fighting retook the old imperial capital. Most of the walled citadel was destroyed.
battles.significance: The bloodiest urban battle of the war, and the site of the Huế massacre — thousands of civilians and officials executed during the occupation, their graves found afterwards.
battles.casualties: Around 600 allied dead; some 5,000 communist; and an estimated 2,800 civilians murdered

battles.name: Siege of Khe Sanh
battles.outcome: Seventy-seven days of siege, broken by the heaviest tactical air support of the war. The base was abandoned five months later anyway.
battles.significance: Westmoreland was certain this was to be another Dien Bien Phu and fought it accordingly. Historians still argue whether it was the real objective or a feint to draw forces away from the cities before Tet.
battles.casualties: Around 700 Americans killed; North Vietnamese losses estimated in the thousands

battles.name: The Tet Offensive

belligerents.side1: North Vietnam and the Viet Cong
belligerents.side2: South Vietnam, United States and allies

battles.victor: Allied military victory; a political defeat for the United States
battles.outcome: Simultaneous attacks on more than a hundred towns during the lunar new year truce. All were retaken; the Viet Cong was destroyed as a fighting force.
battles.significance: The battle that was won and lost at the same time. American commanders had said the end was in sight; a country watching the embassy in Saigon under fire stopped believing them. Public support never recovered.
battles.casualties: Perhaps 45,000 communist dead; around 4,000 American and 5,000 South Vietnamese

battles.name: The Yom Kippur War
battles.victor: Israeli recovery after early Arab gains
battles.outcome: A surprise crossing of the Suez Canal on the holiest day of the Jewish year, and a counter-attack that ended with Israeli armour on the Cairo road.
battles.significance: Broke the invincibility won in 1967 on both sides — enough of a shock to Israel, and enough of a restored standing to Egypt, to make Camp David possible five years later. It also triggered the oil embargo that reordered the world economy.
battles.casualties: Around 2,700 Israeli dead; Arab losses perhaps 15,000

battles.name: The Fall of Saigon
battles.outcome: Tanks through the palace gates, and the last helicopters off the embassy roof. South Vietnam surrendered unconditionally.
battles.significance: The end of thirty years of war in Vietnam, and of American involvement in it. The country was reunified the following year.
battles.casualties: Light by the standards of the war; the city largely fell without a siege

battles.name: The Falklands War
battles.outcome: A task force sailed eight thousand miles, landed at San Carlos, walked across the island and took Stanley in ten weeks.
battles.significance: The last war fought by a European power alone and at that distance. It ended the Argentine junta within days, and remade British politics for a decade.

battles.name: Battle of Cuito Cuanavale
battles.outcome: South African and UNITA attacks failed to take the town, and Cuban reinforcements pushed south-west towards the Namibian border. Negotiations opened within months.
battles.significance: The largest battle fought in Africa since the Second World War. It led directly to Namibian independence and to South Africa's withdrawal from the region — and is still claimed as a victory by both sides.
battles.casualties: Estimates differ sharply; likely several thousand dead in all

battles.name: Operation Desert Storm
battles.outcome: Five weeks of air attack, then a hundred hours of ground war that cleared Kuwait and stopped short of Baghdad.
battles.significance: The first war the world watched live, and the demonstration of precision air power that every military since has been built around — or against.
battles.casualties: Around 300 coalition dead; Iraqi military losses estimated in the tens of thousands

battles.name: Annexation of Crimea
battles.outcome: Russian forces seized the peninsula in a near-bloodless operation; the annexation is not internationally recognised.
battles.significance: Opened the Russo-Ukrainian war — the first annexation of one European country's territory by another since 1945, and the prelude to the 2022 full-scale invasion.

battles.name: Battle of Kyiv
battles.outcome: The Russian drive on the capital was fought to a standstill and withdrew after five weeks.
battles.significance: Saved the Ukrainian state in the opening weeks of the full-scale invasion and reshaped the whole war.
battles.casualties: Thousands on both sides; contested figures

battles.name: Kherson counteroffensive
battles.outcome: Russian forces abandoned the west bank of the Dnipro; Kherson was liberated on 11 November 2022.
battles.significance: The only regional capital taken by Russia in 2022 was recovered — a turning point of the year.

battles.name: Siege of Mariupol
battles.outcome: The port city fell after a three-month siege ending at the Azovstal steelworks; the city was largely destroyed.
battles.significance: One of the war's bloodiest sieges — a symbol of resistance and of the war's cost to civilians.

battles.name: Battle of Bakhmut
battles.outcome: After ten months of attritional fighting the ruined city fell; both armies were bled severely.
battles.significance: The longest and bloodiest battle of the war — trench warfare on a scale Europe had not seen since 1945.
battles.casualties: Tens of thousands on both sides

battles.name: Battle of Changping
battles.outcome: After a two-year stand-off, Qin surrounded the Zhao army; most of the Zhao prisoners were executed.
battles.significance: Called the greatest and longest battle of antiquity. Zhao never recovered its manpower, and Qin's road to unifying China lay open.
battles.casualties: Records of the Grand Historian (written over a century later): c. 450,000 Zhao and 250,000 Qin dead

battles.name: Battle of Handan
battles.outcome: The Zhao capital held out until Wei and Chu armies arrived and drove Qin off.
battles.significance: One of Qin's few great defeats after its reforms — it delayed the unification of China by a generation.

battles.name: Battle of Fei River
battles.outcome: A small Jin army routed a much larger Former Qin host after a feigned retreat turned into panic.
battles.significance: It kept southern China out of Former Qin's hands and the north–south split of China lasted another two centuries.

battles.name: Battle of Badr
battles.outcome: Muhammad's smaller force defeated the Meccan army near the wells of Badr.
battles.significance: The first major battle of early Islam; it greatly raised Muhammad's standing in Arabia.
battles.casualties: About 14 Muslims and about 70 Meccans killed

battles.name: Battle of Karbala
battles.outcome: Husayn, grandson of Muhammad, and most of his small band were killed by an Umayyad army.
battles.significance: A defining moment in the Sunni–Shia split; it is mourned every year on Ashura.

battles.name: Battle of Kosovo
battles.outcome: Both Prince Lazar and Sultan Murad I died; both armies were badly hurt.
battles.significance: Serbia was left too weak to resist the Ottomans for long. The battle became central to Serbian identity.

battles.name: Battle of Chaldiran
battles.outcome: Ottoman cannon and muskets broke the Safavid cavalry.
battles.significance: It fixed a rough Ottoman–Persian border for centuries and showed the power of gunpowder armies.
battles.casualties: Uncertain; several thousand on each side

battles.name: Battle of Okehazama
battles.outcome: Oda Nobunaga's small force made a surprise attack in a storm and killed Imagawa Yoshimoto.
battles.significance: It launched Nobunaga's rise towards uniting Japan.

battles.name: Battle of Talikota
battles.outcome: The allied sultanates defeated Vijayanagara and later sacked its capital, Hampi.
battles.significance: It ended the last great Hindu empire of south India.

battles.name: Battle of Nagashino
battles.outcome: Massed musketeers behind fences cut down the charging Takeda cavalry.
battles.significance: A famous early use of firearms on a large scale in Japan.

battles.name: Battle of Myeongnyang
battles.outcome: Admiral Yi Sun-sin, with 13 ships, used a narrow fast-flowing strait to beat a much bigger Japanese fleet.
battles.significance: It stopped the Japanese navy from supporting its army on land.
battles.casualties: Korean losses light; about 30 Japanese ships destroyed or damaged

battles.name: Third Battle of Panipat
battles.outcome: Ahmad Shah Durrani's army crushed the Marathas in one of the largest battles of the 18th century.
battles.significance: It halted Maratha expansion in the north and helped open the way for British power in India.

battles.name: Battle of Boyacá
battles.outcome: Bolívar's army, fresh from crossing the Andes, captured most of the royalist force.
battles.significance: It won independence for what is now Colombia.
battles.casualties: About 13 patriots and 100 royalists killed; about 1,600 royalists captured

battles.name: Battle of Pichincha
battles.outcome: Fought on the slopes of the Pichincha volcano above Quito.
battles.significance: It freed what is now Ecuador from Spanish rule.

battles.name: Battle of Puebla
battles.outcome: A smaller Mexican army beat back the French attack on the forts above Puebla.
battles.significance: A morale-boosting win remembered as Cinco de Mayo, though France later took Mexico City.

battles.name: Battle of Ulundi
battles.outcome: A British square with rifles, cannon and Gatling guns broke the Zulu attack, then burned the royal kraal.
battles.significance: The last major battle of the Anglo-Zulu War; it ended Zulu independence.
battles.casualties: About 13 British and 500 or more Zulu killed
